title: Bid carries only iurl (no adm, no nurl); preview falls back to the QA thumbnail

source.name: IAB OpenRTB 2.6 — Bid.iurl ("URL without cache-busting to an image that is representative of the content of the campaign for ad quality/safety checking")
source.notes: iurl is explicitly a QA/ad-quality field per spec, not a delivery markup field; this pair is deliberately built without adm/nurl to exercise that boundary.

modifications: All auction, bid, creative, site, app and publisher identifiers are synthetic.
All domains use reserved .test names; no real user IDs, IP addresses, consent strings or tracker endpoints.
All text and SVG artwork are original; no public creative copied.
device.ip is the documentation-only address 192.0.2.11; OS values describe a synthetic test device.
The image at iurl is the well-known 1x1 transparent PNG (public-domain minimal PNG, used only as an inert pixel, not copied creative art).
provenance.sanitized: Only synthetic identifiers, original fixture creatives, reserved domains and TEST-NET addresses. No live tokens, subscriber IDs or real tracking URLs.

pairApplicability.note: Every response bid references an offered impression; auction identifiers match.

specNotes: Protocol validity is based on cited fields, not on current Core output. Optional-field warnings do not make this pair invalid.

response.bid.payload_missing (WARNING) is spec-accurate here, not a false positive: per §4.2.3 iurl is a QA/ad-quality field, never a delivery-markup substitute for adm/nurl. This bid genuinely carries no ad markup.

The preview's iurl fallback (public/ortbtools.app.js findAdm) is a documented convenience beyond the spec, not a spec-mandated rendering path — do not read a rendered thumbnail as proof the bid had markup.
Browser assertions are proposed observables; this corpus has not been run in a browser.

Assert the fallback element has image.complete and naturalWidth > 0 (the 1x1 PNG decodes to a real, if tiny, raster image) — this is the "rendered via iurl fallback" proof, not a marker-text proof, since the QA thumbnail carries no label text.
notes: Core observations in the source archive were deliberately excluded from expectations. Protocol metadata may describe a vendor-specific 2.x carrier; it does not claim a normative minor-version inference.

preview.limitation: iurl is a QA thumbnail, not delivery markup; the tool renders it only as a documented convenience fallback.
